before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: the practice's own visit types only (a new patient consult, a laser treatment, an injection, an imaging scan, or an eye problem visit), never a symptom typed into the AI
a vision or medical plan (its name only) or paying yourself
after_time: anything the practice should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a care home visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the ophthalmologist
secure_page_only: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the plan card
health history: medicines, blood thinners, allergies, eye conditions, diabetes
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
intake_questions.never_asked: symptoms, reasons or results are never asked or typed in the AI chat
intake_questions.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)

stop.words: sudden vision loss, sudden flashes of light, or a shadow or curtain across the vision
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911. Don't wait for an eye visit.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words are repeated if a same-day request is declined, and if it starts before a booked visit (the visit stays booked and the owner is told)

stop.words: a chemical splash in the eye, or something stuck in it
stop.say: Rinse a chemical splash with clean running water right away, and call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 or 911. Don't rub something stuck in the eye: go to the emergency room or call 911.
stop.booking: no booking; the words are fixed and the same for everyone

stop.words: an eye hit hard or cut, or sudden bad eye pain with a headache or throwing up
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911.

go_on.words: red, itchy, sore or dry eyes with nothing else
go_on.what: matched to the practice's own eye problem visit; Rosie never judges how urgent it is, and same-day times need the owner's OK

safety_and_stop_words.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.name: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before any test), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered, some services only, not covered, or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free)

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; sent within 1 business day (the example practice's rule), or sooner where the rules require it
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: A signed procedure consent
steps.when: on the secure page, before the laser or injection visit, with the price and the deposit shown first
steps.who: every procedure patient, and the parent or guardian for a child
steps.result: not signed by the procedure visit: the visit waits; Sam moves it or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The care home's OK
steps.who: the host place agrees to host the visits
steps.result: no OK: no times at that place

first_steps_and_forms.prep: bring your glasses, your medicine list and a photo ID; a dilated exam blurs the eyes for a few hours, so a ride home is needed; at a care home: the medicine list ready with the nurse

staff.skills: ophthalmologists: exams, laser treatments, injections, eye surgery referrals, low-vision aids and prescriptions; ophthalmic technicians: pre-tests, imaging, drop teaching and the work the state allows; only people cleared for mobile visits go to care homes and schools
staff.licenses_or_certificates: each ophthalmologist's own medical license, per state; an ophthalmic technician's own license only where the state licenses technicians
staff.supervision: a technician's pre-tests are read by the ophthalmologist; which tests a technician may run comes from the state form (a switch)
staff.who_oks: the owner OKs same-day eye problem times, quotes over $500, and anything a technician flags
staff.stand_in: a technician out: the ophthalmologist runs the pre-tests, or new times; the ophthalmologist out: another ophthalmologist takes the visit, or new times with no fee

children_and_age.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)
children_and_age.minors_texts: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
children_and_age.minors_rules: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)

visit.check_in: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or school: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or staff member named on the booking
visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the ophthalmologist's notes, scans and prescriptions stay in the practice's own records, never in Rosie or a text
visit.changes_at_visit: an extra test or drops are priced and OK'd before they're done; a medical problem found at a routine exam may move the visit to the medical plan, with the share shown first; a laser or an injection is booked as its own visit only with the patient's yes
visit.before_work: the technician does the pre-tests (vision, eye pressure, imaging) first; the ophthalmologist reads the health history and checks for changes before any procedure

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: each ophthalmologist holds their own medical license from the state's medical board; an ophthalmic technician holds one only where the state licenses technicians
license.who: each person; the practice too where the state's form registers eye practices or their owners
license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply, or the owner sends it; the practice's registration and any mobile permit number come from the owner. The owner may leave a number out
license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it; the owner states it, and Rosie does not check it

never_in_a_text: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, the results, the medicines or the ophthalmologist's name (when the ophthalmologist comes to a care home, school or home, the name stays, for the door check); scans and results never go through Rosie
